papers.title: Electrochemical surface modification of Ti6Al4V: positioning electrochemical machining as a low-valence dissolution pathway for enhanced performance
papers.abstract: The automotive, aerospace, biomedical, and other engineering sectors make substantial use of Ti6Al4V titanium alloy, known for its high strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility, but it often suffers from poor tribological performance and low surface hardness. To increase durability, a variety of surface modification techniques have been investigated, including chemical etching, shot peening, thermal oxidation, laser surface texturing, and physical vapor deposition. However, these methods frequently entail high thermal input and mechanical stress with limited control over surface chemistry. Electrochemical methods, on the other hand, allow uniform and precise alteration of surface morphology without thermal or mechanical damage. Among these, anodization and plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) facilitate hardening and stress-free surfaces but suffer from passive film formation, porosity and micro-cracks, while electrochemical polishing (ECP) yields much better surface finish but at high energy cost and causes passive film formation. In this review, electrochemical machining (ECM), typically viewed as a subtractive method for material removal, is reevaluated as a process for both material removal and functional surface tailoring. Despite its application for removing material, ECM promotes valence-controlled dissolution that favours the formation of lower oxidation states of titanium. It also inhibits the formation of passive films and enables the formation of atomically smooth surfaces. The present study provides a novel theoretical framework for customizing Ti6Al4V surfaces with improved functional and morpho­logical properties by integrating ECM with anodization, PEO and ECP within the broader paradigm of electrochemical surface engineering.

summary_en.motivation: This review aims to consolidate electrochemical surface modification techniques for Ti6Al4V to overcome its poor tribological performance and low surface hardness.
summary_en.method: The authors propose a theoretical framework integrating electrochemical machining (ECM) with anodization, plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO), and electrochemical polishing (ECP) under a unified electrochemical surface engineering paradigm.
summary_en.result: ECM enables valence-controlled dissolution favoring lower oxidation states, inhibits passive film formation, and produces atomically smooth surfaces with enhanced functional and morphological properties.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation is provided; the work is a conceptual review and theoretical framework.

papers.title: Additively manufactured oxygen-doped TiZrNb medium-entropy alloy with enhanced corrosion resistance and apatite-forming ability
papers.abstract: The development of load-bearing metallic implants requires an uncommon combination of mechanical compatibility, corrosion resistance in physiological environments, and biocompatibility that supports stable integration with host tissues. In this study, we investigate an oxygen-doped TiZrNb medium-entropy alloy (~1 at.% O) fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) and evaluate its mechanical compatibility and bioactivity-relevant interfacial stability in simulated body fluid (SBF) on the plane perpendicular to the building direction, alongside the previously reported strength-ductility synergy. Nanoindentation reveals a low elastic modulus of ~80.86 GPa, substantially lower than that of commercially pure Ti and Ti-6Al-4V, indicating improved elastic matching with bone and reduced propensity for stress shielding. Electrochemical testing in SBF demonstrates markedly enhanced passivation of the additively manufactured alloy relative to its cast counterpart, evidenced by a low corrosion current density (i corr = 1.52 × 10 -8 A·cm -2 ) and a high charge-transfer resistance (R ct = 207.6 kΩ·cm 2 ). In vitro apatite-forming tests show that the L-PBF surface develops dense and uniformly distributed Ca-P-O-rich deposits, suggesting an improved mineralization capability. Collectively, these results establish an additive manufacturing pathway to integrate bone-friendlier elasticity with robust corrosion/mineralization performance in TiZrNb-based alloys, supporting the promise of L-PBF TiZrNb-O for next-generation, patient-specific load-bearing implants.

papers.title: Effect of annealing temperature on mechanical properties of welds of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy
papers.abstract: This study investigates the microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti-6Al-4V welds at different annealing temperatures, aiming to clarify the role of temperature in joining thin-walled titanium alloy pipes for aerospace applications. It is found that (1) with the same annealing temperature, Widmanstätten structures are observed in the welds by laser welding, and no Widmanstätten structure is observed in the welds by TIG welding. (2) The joint performance depends on the average grain size and the dislocation of the weld. When the annealing temperature is set as 650 °C, the tensile strength of the weld by laser is slightly higher (i.e., 0.9%) than that of the weld by TIG, and the microhardness of the weld by laser shows no difference from that of the weld by TIG. The average grain size of the weld by laser is 3.48% higher than that of the weld by TIG. The KAMave of the weld by laser is 14.8% lower than that of the weld by TIG. (3) When the specimens are joined by laser welding and the annealing temperature is increased from 650 to 800 °C, the weld microstructure transforms into a basketweave structure. Both microhardness and tensile strength of the weld are decreased significantly. The average grain size of the weld is increased by 8.73%, and the KAMave of the weld is decreased by 28.3%. In summary, the impact of the annealing temperature on the joint performance of the weld by laser welding is significantly greater than that of the weld by TIG.

papers.title: Study on the influence of tool structure on the gyroscopic milling performance of CFRP/Ti-6Al-4V stacked materials
papers.abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP)/titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) stacked materials have been widely used in the aerospace field due to their excellent mechanical performance. However, owing to the differences in both mechanical and thermal properties between CFRP and Ti-6Al-4V, the machining characteristics of CFRP/Ti-6Al-4V stacked materials are significantly different from those of single-material components. Therefore, selecting appropriate tool structures and machining processes is an effective approach to improving hole quality. This paper proposes a gyroscopic milling process method and conducts comparative experiments on hole-milling using three milling cutters with different corner radii, performed on a self-developed gyroscopic milling actuator. A multi-point offset thermocouple configuration in both axial and radial directions is proposed for cutting temperature measurement. The influence patterns of tool structure and machining parameters on cutting temperature, axial force, and hole-making quality are analyzed. The results indicate that increasing the spindle speed while decreasing the orbital speed and feed rate can effectively reduce the axial force during gyroscopic milling of stacked materials. As the tool corner radius increases, the cutting temperature and axial force demonstrate certain reductions in all machining zones - whether in CFRP, Ti-6Al-4V, or the two-body material machining zone. Compared to the other two milling cutters, the tool with a 2 mm corner radius strengthens the deformation resistance of the residual material at the hole exit zone during machining, thereby achieving a more ideal hole exit quality.

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the influence of tool corner radius on the gyroscopic milling performance of CFRP/Ti-6Al-4V stacked materials to improve hole quality.
summary_en.method: Comparative experiments were conducted using three milling cutters with different corner radii on a self-developed gyroscopic milling actuator, with a multi-point thermocouple configuration for temperature measurement.
